reason: Answer (reply 3, 8) is only Darwin's farewell and signature to Gray's valediction (para 4); no content.
Reply 2 answers Sedgwick's complaint about the concluding chapter's confident tone and appeal to young men (para 5).
Reply 1 on Leschenaultia pollen tubes and the stigmatic surface takes up Hooker's para 1 on Goodenia flowers and the viscid surface.
Reply 2 is mostly about the American edition (paras 1-3), but it also asks Gray to fix 'self-fertilise itself', which comes from para 7, a separate topic.
Reply 1 thanks Sclater for his list of Galapagos birds, which is the whole of the question (paras 1-7, 9).
Reply 2 names Wollaston as the Annals reviewer and repeats the Bishop of Oxford's 'unphilosophical' remark, which answers paras 4-5.
Reply 3 thanks Galton for the 'other notes' he mentions in the question and comments on sexual selection, which those notes prompted.
Reply 6 welcomes the criticisms Gray says he will send later about gaps in the evidence (para 4).
Reply 4 says Waterhouse wants to see the worker-to-drone cell gradation, which answers Smith's offer of his comb piece in para 1.
Reply 5 asks Gray to thank Wyman for offering hints and regrets Dana's illness, which answers paras 13, 15 and 17.
Reply 1 thanks Bunbury for praise (para 1) but also regrets that he is not converted, which answers para 2's 'I am not convinced'.
Replies 3, 4 and 6 answer Gray's best and weak points (eye, sterility), his non-committal review and his praise (paras 6-12, 20).
Reply 1 answers Hooker's approval of the book in para 1 and the postscript in para 7.
Reply 3 comments on Hooker being settled in his Kew house and his heavy workload, which answers para 5.
Reply 1 opens with Darwin's own unprompted news of a Madagascar hippopotamus tooth, repeated in reply 2; it never answers the reindeer antler question.
Reply 2 identifies the wren (para 8) but also discusses the Zenaida occurring on the mainland, an item that is not in the question.
Reply 1 thanks Galton for the pleasure his congratulations on the book gave him (para 1).
Reply 4 is only 'Many thanks for your pleasant note' and a signature, matching the valediction in para 7.
Reply 6 acknowledges the Asa Gray letter enclosed with para 1 and says he is too sick to read it yet.
Reply 1 thanks the booksellers for their French dictionary advice (para 1) and says he will call about it.
Reply 2 on Pompilus and Calathus wing gradations answers para 2, not the apology and signature given as the question (para 3).
Reply 3 says whether Darwin can attend the Club and explains his health, which answers Hooker's para 6 about the Club.
Reply 6 is only a valediction and signature and says nothing about the Australian Drosera in para 4.
Reply 3 is closing formula regretting Sedgwick's 'disapprobation and ridicule' (paras 2-4); it ignores his health and heaven remarks (paras 6-7).
Reply 1 thanks Spencer and praises his framing of the theory as a hypothesis that explains many facts, which answers paras 1-5.
Replies 5 and 6 are only renewed thanks, kind remembrances and a signature, answering Galton's closing regards; no content.
Reply 1 admits the Agassiz blunder (para 14) but mainly sends the Historical Preface and corrections, which answers other paragraphs.
Reply 1 promises to measure the Jamaican bee cells once Smith makes his final identification, which answers para 1.
Reply 5 asks about a Russian translation of the Origin; the question is only a signature and address (paras 4-5), which could not prompt it.
Reply 1 thanks Gray for his letter to Hooker, and reply 4 also covers Agassiz and H. D. Rogers; only part concerns Wyman's praise (para 3).
The answer about the 'dignity of man' does not occur in Darwin's reply to Carus, which discusses the preface and Eozoon; wrong letter.
Replies 2 and 3 cover the American edition, sending new matter, Gray's review and answering Agassiz, which answers paras 1-2.
Reply 2 praises Ramsay's general arguments against the immutability of species, set out in paras 1-2.
Reply 4 thanks Thwaites for the Lantana report and urges a list of Ceylon's naturalised plants, which answers para 4.
Replies 3-5 give Darwin's facts on curved styles and nectaries, including Rhododendron, which answers Hooker's paras 3-4.
Replies 1-2 answer Thwaites's objections on beauty, forms not advancing and degeneration (paras 1-3).
The answer (eye, sterility, review by a non-convert) is not in Darwin's reply to Hooker; it comes from the Gray correspondence.
Reply 5 is only 'With hearty thanks for your letter' and a signature; it ignores the Ceylon invitation (para 5).
Reply 7 answers Hooker's remarks that natural selection explains too much (paras 3-5).
Reply 2 accepts Galton's correction about the Rhinoceros on p. 68 given in the question.
Reply 2 asks to hear more about Owen avowing the Review and compares how Owen treats Hooker and Darwin, which answers para 2.
Reply 1 answers the edition and money (paras 1-3); reply 2 adds Darwin's news of Boott, Zoonomia, Owen, converts, Harvey and Macmillan.
The answer about Bates' paper and 'selfish dog' does not occur in Darwin's reply to Rolle; wrong letter.
Replies 2-3 praise Spencer's population pamphlet (para 3) and ask whether to return it.
Reply 3 gives Darwin's opinion of Wallace's Linnean paper, answering Lyell's paras 6-7.
Replies 2 and 7 answer points on representative species, hybridism and vera causa that are not in para 2, which covers only converts and pièces justificatives.
Reply 3 takes up Huxley's second objection in para 7, on why variation occurs if external conditions matter little.
Replies 5-6 are Darwin's own news (climbers work, Haeckel's letter) and do not answer Hooker's paras 1, 4, 5 or 7 on health and examinerships.
Reply 1 answers Sedgwick's disapproval that the book is false and mischievous and his shock (paras 1-4).
Reply 6 regrets Lady Hooker's bone inflammation, which answers para 3 on Hooker's bedridden mother.
Reply 1 thanks Sclater and discusses Otus and Zenaida, which answers his offer in para 3 to examine those birds.
Reply 1 thanks Lyell and discusses Bravard's fossil mammals and Palaeotherium Paranense, which answers paras 2-3.
Reply 2 answers Bentham (para 3), but its A. Gray speculation and J. E. Gray's attack are Darwin's own material, not prompted by paras 2-3.
Reply 2's 'nunc dimittis' relief at Huxley's verdict answers the whole letter (paras 1-11).
